era_setting.place: Lahaina, Maui County, Hawaii, USA; also Kula and upcountry Maui, the Maui Emergency Management Agency operations centre in Wailuku, and the Hawaii state capitol in Honolulu
era_setting.notes: The centre of gravity is 06:37 to about 18:00 on 08 August 2023, on Maui. The film reaches back only as far as the documentary record it quotes -- county and state hazard-mitigation and wildfire reports, utility filings and prior brush fires from about 2014 onward -- and forward to the current status of the litigation. This is a CONTEMPORARY setting, so modern stock is period-correct, and that is this episode's structural advantage. What is wrong here is REGISTER and PLACE, not period. WRONG AND FORBIDDEN IN ANY CUT: the holiday register in every form -- turquoise water, white sand, sunset palms, resorts, pools, luaus, surfing, drone-over-hotel, cocktails, honeymooners, cruise ships. Maui footage on every shelf is holiday footage and it will be offered for every query in this episode. The era-neutral register of this film is grey smoke, a two-lane shoreline road, ash, corrugated steel, melted aluminium, chain-link fence and a standing stone wall -- not scenery. ALSO OUT OF PLACE: mainland-US downtowns, highway signage and vegetation that reads as continental (a Midwest main street, a Texas interstate, a pine or conifer forest, snow); European and Asian streets, EU number plates, right-hand-drive traffic; megacity skylines; desert. Hawaii IS the United States, so US flags, US plates and US uniforms are correct here -- what is wrong is a mainland STREET standing in for a Pacific town. The burning vegetation is dry non-native grass on old plantation land and low scrub, not conifer crown fire. Hawaiian cultural imagery -- hula, lei-making, ceremony, kahili, petroglyphs -- may never be used as decoration or as an establishing flourish; it appears only where the narration is about it and the record supports it. The word 'paradise' does not appear in this film. OUT OF PERIOD: pre-2000 vehicles as the ordinary traffic of 2023, CRT televisions, rotary telephones, pre-digital newsrooms. footage_review_required is true and a labelled contact sheet must be opened by a person before any clip enters a cut.

forbidden_claims: That sounding the sirens would have saved lives, reduced the death toll, or changed the outcome. No source establishes that counterfactual. The film may state what the sirens are for, that they were not sounded, and what officials said about why -- it may never complete the sentence with a consequence the record does not carry.

That any named official, agency or employee is at fault, negligent, or criminally responsible. Statements about the siren decision are quoted verbatim and attributed to the person who made them and the date they made them, with their position and current legal status stated in the same breath. No narration line, caption, figure or thumbnail may carry an implication of guilt.

Any assertion, hint, rhetorical question or unexplained gap about the cause of the fire. The origin and cause are on the record and the film cites the origin-and-cause investigation directly. The film never says the cause is unknown, disputed among unnamed people, or 'still being asked about'. Raising a question and not answering it is the register of the directed-energy-weapon material this topic sits next to, and this film must be impossible to mistake for it.
That the fire was deliberately set, that anyone profited by design from the destruction, or that the rebuilding, land sales or zoning that followed were the purpose of the fire.

That the utility caused the fire, stated flatly and without attribution. What the utility has acknowledged, what the investigation concluded, and what remains contested must each be given as what it is, with its source and its date.

That a delay or refusal over stream water caused the town to burn or caused any death. The water-access dispute and the diversion of streams are on the record and are part of a live argument; both are stated with attribution as documented facts and are never used as an implied cause, and never as colour.

Any victim's name, face, likeness, voice or personal detail. About a hundred people died and the film names none of them. No burned vehicle presented as containing anyone. No human remains, no body bags, no memorial carrying a face.

Any figure for the death toll, the number of missing, acreage, wind speed, structures destroyed, siren count, response times or settlement amount that is not in the FACTS_LEDGER with a primary source and the date it was current. The death toll was revised repeatedly after August 2023 and the film uses the ledger's figure with its date, never an early one.
Any statement about the status of the settlement or any lawsuit that has not been re-verified from a primary or named-outlet source on the day of writing. This is a live case.

That climate change, or any other single factor, caused this fire. Causation in the record is layered -- weather, fuel, land use, infrastructure, warning -- and the film does not collapse it into one line.
notes: v003, 2026-08-22. Every declared NUMBER is still byte-for-byte v001's. The change is the MEMBERSHIP of `people_plates`, and the reason is a defect found by looking rather than by a gate: v002 listed 24 ids taken from the image order's P flags, and SIX of those 24 prompts never asked for a human at all. check_episode_inputs counts the declared list, so it would have reported 24 people plates for a film with eighteen -- a false green on a floor that exists because a town with no faces is a town the audience does not believe in. Resolution: H121, H125 and H126 are empty BY DESIGN (the empty chair, the empty corridor, the empty bench) and were de-flagged rather than have a person forced into a frame whose whole meaning is that nobody is in it; H058, H095 and H099 had a figure written into their prompts and are re-ordered; and H133-H135 are new, taken from FILM_BIBLE v001 section 11's own people list, which named a figure at a window looking mauka, a lineman on a pole and a hand closing a folder -- three concepts that never reached the order. The list below is GENERATED from the order's P flags, and every one of the 24 now has a human in its prompt. v002, 2026-08-21. Identical to v001 in EVERY declared number -- runtime_seconds, script_words, figure_beats_per_act, distinct_video_assets, people_plates_min, target_cut_sec, audio_layers, era_setting, forbidden_subjects and forbidden_claims are byte-for-byte the v001 values and were NOT re-tuned to suit the script. The single change is the ADDITION of `people_plates`, which v001 could not carry because the plate ids did not exist until EP75_lahaina_CODEX_BATCH_A.v001.md was written. The gate found the gap, not a person: check_episode_inputs.py reported '0 P### people stills against the 24 this episode declares', because with no `people_plates` list it falls back to counting filenames that start with P -- and this episode's people plates are H004, H005, H008 ... The schema field exists precisely for that case and EP62-EP66 all declare it. The 24 ids below are GENERATED from the P flags in the image order, not typed, so the two cannot drift. Derived 2026-08-21 from EP75_lahaina_HANDOVER.v001 and PD_ONE_PASS_PRODUCTION_SPEC.v3. runtime_seconds [1740,1920] = 29:00-32:00, the batch band EP72 was built to and delivered inside (measured 29:44). script_words [4900,5400] is NOT the standard's [4400,4900]: EP72 measured 191.7 raw wpm against the registry's 171.79 model, so 29:00-32:00 of narration at the measured pace needs more words, not fewer -- 1740s x 0.9 narration share = 26.1 min x 188 wpm = 4,907; 1920s x 0.9 = 28.8 min x 188 wpm = 5,414, rounded to [4900,5400]. This band is a starting frame only: per spec v3 6.6/6.7 the script is sized with gen_narration_case.py --dry-run and confirmed with --measure-section ACT_1 before it is written to length, and check_script_length is not used for sizing because it counts HTML citation comments as spoken words. distinct_video_assets = 265 from PD_EPISODE_SPEC_STANDARD.v001's formula runtime x 0.65 / 4.5 at the 1,830s midpoint (1,830 x 0.65 = 1,189.5; / 4.5 = 264.3 -> 265). audio_layers = 4 per spec v3 row 4 (the finisher builds four; the standard's default of 2 is the historical artefact). people_plates_min = 24, above EP72's 20, because this film's people are ordinary residents, dispatchers, linemen and firefighters rather than three named defendants, and the plate pool has to carry a whole town without repeating. target_cut_sec 3.8 as EP72. mandatory_stills is deliberately absent: no stills exist for this episode yet, and the field is populated only when purpose-made stills exist to cover a gap. R3: about a hundred real deaths in 2023, living families, and litigation that is still moving -- forbidden_claims is the legally load-bearing part of this spec, and the first three entries exist because this topic shares its search terms with an active conspiracy audience and must be impossible to mistake for that material.
